title: typocasual contact sheet data
description: Contract for public/data.json. This file is the single source of truth for the shape of the site's content. scripts/check.mjs validates data.json against it and runs before every deploy.

meta.description: Page-level copy. Not currently rendered — the masthead copy is in index.html.

filters.description: The filter buttons, in order. Each id matches a frame's `kind` or `stage`. `all` is special and always matches everything.

items.description: The frames on the contact sheet, in display order.

linksHead.description: Heading copy for the outbound link sheet. Omit to leave that section empty.

links.description: Outbound links rendered as preview cards under the sheet.

item.description: One frame. `kind` decides how the window is drawn; the fields it needs are enforced below.

kind.description: note = text card, spec = type specimen, plate = generated concrete photograph.

stage.description: Shown in the frame badge. Must agree with `growth`: see the bands in scripts/check.mjs.

growth.description: How overgrown the frame is. 0 = bare concrete, 1 = buried. Drives the moss height.

medium.description: Shown in the caption bar and lightbox, e.g. "Silver gelatin".

subject.description: Plates only. Shown in the lightbox meta line.

body.description: note only. Clamped to 7 lines in the frame, shown whole in the lightbox.

sample.description: spec only. The large glyphs, e.g. "Aa".

stack.description: spec only. A CSS font-family value, e.g. "\"Lora\", Georgia, serif".

specimen.description: spec only. The sample line of text.

seed.description: plate and link cards. Picks the composition. Same seed always produces the same image; the archetype rotates by seed % 6.

link.description: One outbound link card. The preview shows a generated plate plus a monogram, with the destination favicon layered on top if it loads — so a dead link still renders.

url.description: Must be absolute and https. The hostname is derived from this for the domain label and the favicon lookup.
